back: Hardware that converts the results of processing into images, printed pages, sound or movement.
An output device that turns an electrical signal into movement (motor, valve, solenoid, pump).
LCD: liquid crystals control a backlight (often LEDs). LED screen: each pixel's LEDs give out their own light.
Millions of tilting micro-mirrors (one per pixel) and a spinning colour wheel; high contrast.
Light split into red, green and blue beams through three LCD panels, combined by a prism; bright colours.
Drum charged → laser forms electrostatic image → toner attracted → transferred to paper → fuser melts it on.
Moving print head fires ink droplets through nozzles (thermal bubble or piezoelectric crystal); paper moves line by line.
Builds a solid object layer by layer from a digital design (additive manufacturing).
DAC → amplifier → current in a coil in a magnetic field → cone vibrates → sound waves.
